c: Similar to Pentagram, Gorgeous Moon erases enemies on the screen, but no longer destroys pickups. Instead, it generates additional experience. Gorgeous Moon Generation and Erasure phase always deal damage equal to the max health of the enemy. If it is lower than 660, the damage number is overwritten to display it between 655 and 665.
Gorgeous Moon's effect has three phases:
Generation: This phase occurs 3 s after

. As the glyph of Gorgeous Moon appears on the ground, it pulses and chimes. It targets the closest enemies on the screen with a moon beam that can erase them, generating uniquely colored Experience Gems (orange, yellow, magenta) that yield 1 experience next to their usual gem drop. The attack frequency increases over time until the next phase.
Attack frequency starts at 0.75 s for 8 beams, 0.375 s for 4 beams, and 0.2 s for 8 beams, for a total of 20 beams in 9.1 s.

Erasure: This phase occurs 12.1 s after Cooldown. A waxing crescent symbol appears and shatters, erasing all enemies on the screen like Pentagram. This has a 0% chance of destroying items, and enemies erased also drop an extra Experience Gem.

Vacuum: This phase occurs a brief moment after the previous phase. A waning crescent symbol mends from the shattered glyph and disappears, attracting all the gems on the level, identically to the Vacuum effect.

Gorgeous Moon can be affected by Cooldown bonuses, but there is a hardcoded limit of 15 seconds on how often Gorgeous Moon can trigger, which would make Gorgeous Moon active almost all of the time, going through its three phases.
Some enemies are completely unaffected by Gorgeous Moon.
Gorgeous Moon can attack and defeat the otherwise intangible Stalkers and Drowners in
, and
before minute 30, causing them to drop chests.

Since Gorgeous Moon has a 0% chance of destroying Pickups, it is advised to evolve
as soon as possible upon selecting it.
Because some enemies, like
The Reaper or bosses at the 25th minute in most stages, are immune to Gorgeous Moon's effect, it cannot be relied on as your only tool of killing enemies.
To reach Gorgeous Moon's 15 s cooldown limit, a Cooldown bonus of -75% is required.
With
, the vacuum effect can periodically collect all the
Experience Gems and hurl them at enemies. Since the damage of each gem is based of the experience amount, Gorgeous Moon needing
to evolve increases the damage dealt by them, further increased by its Limit Break effect for gems generated by the moon beams.
With Limit Break enabled Gorgeous Moon's

can be leveled up. As with Pentagram and most other weapons when Gorgeous Moon is chosen to level up it will immediately be activated even if currently active. If Gorgeous Moon is the only weapon which can be upgraded through Limit Break, and

is high enough, it can be caught in a self-perpetuating loop resulting in innumerable layered Gorgeous Moon attacks constantly firing. The only ways to break the loop once it's started are to avoid getting any experience and waiting for the game to catch up (
and/or
work) or for the character to die.

Gorgeous Moon most likely is a reference to the

series. The crescent symbol that appears on the ground strongly resembles one of the locket designs from the series. The chime sound effect during its Generation phase is reminiscent of the various sparkle sounds from the anime as well. The name references one of Sailor Moon's attacks, Moon Gorgeous Meditation.
